subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — reserved GPU pool fit & next asks
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Maya Rao <maya@optiscale.com>, Lucas Chen <lucas@optiscale.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — reserved GPU pool fit & next asks

Hi Maya / Lucas —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side so we have aligned next steps and success criteria for evaluating Redwood Dedicated for OptiScale's inference workloads. Please flag anything I missed.

What we heard
- Primary pain: unpredictable token latency and spiky costs from your current multi-tenant endpoints when batch jobs and interactive traffic collide.
- Isolation requirement: regulatory team needs logical separation per business unit (no shared GPU tenancy).
- Predictability: pricing/throughput guarantees for peak-hours (US-East) are critical — they want predictable TPS for inference SLAs.
- Autoscaling: need burst capacity for weekly nightly batches (30–60 min windows) without manual intervention.

Current stack & constraints- Self-hosted Triton + a mix of CPU fallback instances for cheaper workloads.
- Models: mixture of Llama-2-Chat-70B (quantized) for interactive and a 13B reranker for high-throughput scoring.
- KV cache usage for session continuity; large prefix reuse on chat sessions.
- On-prem firewall for audit logs; security team requires SOC2 controls and KMS integration.

Success criteria (what OptiScale cares about)- 95th percentile latency under 250ms for interactive (<= 1024 tokens context) during peak;
- Deterministic cost per 1k tokens for planning;
- Logical isolation per BU + auditable access logs;
- Autoscale that handles 2x baseline TPS within 3 minutes and supports scheduled pre-warming for nightly batches.

Redwood initial fit/notes- Dedicated reserved GPU pools map well to isolation + predictability asks.
- KV/prefix caching will likely reduce token throughput needs for interactive use-cases.
- We need model accuracy/quantization validation for the 70B variant — quantization profile could change peak GPU footprint.

Action items / next steps1) Redwood -> deliver a preliminary sizing & pricing PDF with two configurations: steady-state reserved pool + burstable overlay; include cost estimate and ETA for a pilot. (ETA: 48 business hours) — attached.
2) OptiScale -> share a week of anonymized traffic traces (sampled) and any recent p95 latency reports so we can validate sizing assumptions. Lucas, can you share the telemetry snippet?
3) Security -> OptiScale to share SOC2/infra control checklist items (we support KMS/HSM integrations) so we can produce an evidence map for Private vs Dedicated.
4) Scheduling -> propose a 2-week pilot window in US-East; Redwood will commit to an SLA target for the pilot.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf (attached), optiscale-infra-snippet.json (requested)

I'll follow up with the sizing doc and a short tech note outlining autoscale knobs and prefilling for nightly batches.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — reserved GPU pool fit & next asks

Laura / Rishi —

Quick technical notes from my side after listening in:
- For the Llama-2-Chat-70B quantized path we should assume ~4–6 A100-equivalent GPU hours per 1k concurrent sessions depending on KV cache hit rate; I'll run a micro-benchmark once we get Lucas's trace.
- Autoscaling policy: suggest a warm-pool of N-2 GPUs for fast ramp and instant burst via ephemeral instances. This keeps steady-state cost down but preserves 2x burst inside 3 minutes.
- Networking / isolation: recommend dedicating a VPC per BU and overlaying security groups + private peering; audit logs hook to a central SIEM via syslog or S3 export.

I'll produce a short sizing worksheet and include an option with checkpoint-optimized kernels vs standard (trades cost vs latency). ETA end of day tomorrow.

- Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the proposal.
